Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of requirements I captured:
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 200ms for typical user flows (short responses ~256-512 tokens).
- Worst-case guidance: P95 <= 350ms for larger responses (up to ~2k output tokens) is acceptable if we trade off throughput.
- Concurrent users/throughput: ~120-200 concurrent request window (peak), target sustained concurrency ~100.
- Streaming: streaming responses (chunked / SSE) are required for your live-chat UX for responses >512 tokens.
- Context window: customers will send up to 16k tokens of input in some flows (doc + user prompt); output typically 512-2k tokens depending on flow.

Notes / risks:
- Large input (8k-16k tokens) will increase generation time and I/O; SLOs above assume prefix caching and batched KV cache support.
- If you require P95 <=200ms on 2k-token outputs, we’ll need a dedicated capacity plan and quantization/beam optimizations; otherwise we can hit 200ms on 256-512 token outputs on shared Hosted tiers.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach a short perf snapshot from a comparable customer (see attached CSV) showing P50/P95 token-perf across payload sizes.
2) Can you confirm the fraction of queries that will be >1k input tokens (estimate as a % of traffic)?
3) If streaming is mandatory for those long outputs, confirm whether partial tokens during streaming are acceptable (we send tokens as generated) or you need deterministic chunk sizes.
4) I’ll schedule a short perf/arch sync next week with Rishi (runtime) and Neha (onboarding/infra) to size Dedicated/Private options if needed.

Feel free to edit the summary above — happy to add anything I missed.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and captures our discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Percent of large inputs: roughly 18% of calls will include >8k input tokens (these are full-doc summarization flows); another ~40% are in the 1k-4k range. The remainder are short prompts (~<512 tokens).
- Streaming: yes, streaming is mandatory for any response where output >512 tokens; we prefer partial tokens as generated (SSE) rather than fixed-size chunks.
- SLO tolerance: for the full-doc summarization flow we can accept a higher P95 (up to 500ms) if throughput remains reasonable and cost stays within our projected budget. For interactive chat flows (short prompts) the 200ms P95 target is important.

Next: please confirm whether the streaming + 16k input + 2k output scenario is feasible on a shared Hosted tier, or whether we should evaluate Dedicated. Also please send the perf snapshot you mentioned.

Best,

Alicia — thanks for the extra detail. Quick guidance from our side after a preliminary review of the attached snapshot: 

- Hosted tier: streaming + up to 8k input + 512-1k output is commonly supported with P95 ~180-300ms depending on load; once you push to 16k inputs + 2k outputs the decode time dominates and you’ll likely see P95s in the 400-700ms range on shared capacity.
- Dedicated: with a pinned Dedicated GPU pool (and aggressive batching + KV prefix caching) we can bring P95 down to ~220-300ms for 16k input/2k output in many cases, and reduce variance with autoscaling headroom for peaks.
- Concurrency: the key lever is concurrency vs. batching. If your peak concurrent requests are 120-200 and a significant fraction are large-context runs, Dedicated sizing needs to account for effective batch depth; Rishi will run a quick right-sized estimate.

Action items I’m taking: 
- Attached the perf snapshot (FinCo_perf_snapshot_20270610.csv) - it includes token throughput and P50/P95 across payload sizes for a comparable enterprise customer.
- Rishi: can you run a back-of-envelope for Dedicated sizing (GPU count, target batch config) given these traffic distributions?
- Alicia/Tom: once you confirm the % of >8k calls (Alicia said ~18%) we’ll prep a Dedicated cost estimate and a hosted guidance doc.

I’ll also attach our SLO playbook PDF which outlines fallback policies, prefix caching and streaming best-practices.

-M
